picks.style: late antique riddle-dialogue, plucked lyre and light frame drum, two alternating voices, quick, restless, quicksilver
picks.why: Opportunity on her wheel, winged, bald behind — and gone from your hands while you stand there asking questions.

picks.style: doric war epitaph, low male voices in unison, bone flute and slow drum, austere, stony, unhurried
picks.why: 'Return with this, or upon it' — and the father who tells the mourners to weep for other men's sons.

picks.style: late roman love elegy, soft cithara and low strings, ageing wistful voice, slow, rueful, intimate
picks.why: 'Galla, we grow old' — and the terrible closing bargain: I will take, not what I would, but what I once would.

picks.style: greek tragic monody, solo male voice with aulos and low drum, slow, resolute, sun-struck, final
picks.why: The last speech: the Erinyes summoned, Helios asked to carry the news home, then 'O light! O sacred soil'.

picks.style: greek choral meditation, lyre and soft aulos, calm baritone, cyclical, seasonal, deceptively serene
picks.why: Winter yielding to summer, night to day, the winds letting the sea rest — the great deception speech.

picks.style: soldiers' lament chorus, frame drum and reed pipe, weary massed male voices, slow, damp, homesick
picks.why: No garlands, no wine-cups, no flutes, no love — only heavy dew wetting their hair year after year at Troy.

picks.style: english pastoral song, guitar and recorder, easy tenor, lilting, contented, unhurried
picks.why: 'Busily idle, calmly gay; nor great, nor mean, nor rich, nor poor' — a whole philosophy in four tetrameters.

picks.style: minuet turned reflective, harpsichord and strings, wry baritone, dance tempo, circling, resigned
picks.why: The dance as an image of a life: 'quite tir'd sit down, just where we first begun'.

picks.style: hudibrastic patter song, harpsichord and fiddle, fast comic voice, headlong, clattering, farcical
picks.why: 'Pigs squeak, fowls scream, and green geese flutter' — a country visit as pure comic momentum.

picks.style: english hymn in common metre, chapel organ and small choir, clear female voice, steady, luminous, ascending
picks.why: 'Then swift, to find our Fellow-souls, as Light, we haste away' — already in hymn metre and already a hymn.

picks.style: georgian retirement song, guitar and flute, warm alto, gentle amble, homely, contented
picks.why: The whole wish for a life: a hill, a brook, good neighbours, a useful book, and time to mend one's ways.

picks.style: devotional ode, harpsichord and viol, bright soprano, measured, plain, radiant
picks.why: 'Wisdom is Truth without Disguise: clear as the Sun in cloudless Skies' — plain and hard to improve on.

picks.style: latin farewell song, solo cithara over a low drone, young resolved male voice, steady, valedictory, brightening
picks.why: Away with the rhetoricians — sails set for the blessed harbours, and the reluctant goodbye to the sweet Camenae.

picks.style: roman pastoral miniature, single reed pipe and soft strings, quiet tenor, tender, small-scale, homely
picks.why: 'Little farm, that were Siro's, and you, poor little field' — a poet commending his father to a scrap of land.

picks.style: roman moral elegy, low strings and slow drum, grave baritone, stately then abrupt, stark
picks.why: The man who had shaken the globe collapsing headlong: 'the deceitful hour, in a moment of time, wears away mortal things'.

picks.style: archaic greek elegy, lyre over a low drone, grave male voice, measured, declamatory, earth-rooted
picks.why: Solon calling black Earth as witness that he tore up her boundary-stones and brought the sold-away home.

picks.style: archaic greek elegy, aulos and lyre, sorrowing male voice, slow, admonitory, unresolved
picks.why: 'I stood casting my strong shield about both, and allowed neither to win an unjust victory.'

picks.style: athenian drinking skolion, lyre passed hand to hand, lead voice with answering chorus, short, convivial, defiant
picks.why: Two real drinking songs — the lament for Leipsydrion and 'pour for Cedon too, servant, and do not forget'.

picks.style: greek cult hymn, girls' chorus with lyre and aulos, bright unison voices, processional, joyous, refrain-driven
picks.why: Only candidate, but it ends on a real cult refrain: 'hail, Paean Apollo! hail, Titus our saviour!'
